text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BRAZIL HITS NEW RECORD IN CAPITAL RAISED OVERSEAS

Brazil already this year has beaten its annual record for capital raised abroad, with a nominal $13.6 billion raised via 193 issues up to yesterday. The figure includes 25 types of short-, medium and long-term debt but not stock issues or bank loans.
-- VOTORANTIM AND CSN ACQUIRE JOAO SANTOS CEMENT FIRM

Brazil's Votorantim group and Cia Siderurgica Nacional (CSN) decided yesterday to invest 26.1 million reais each to acquire control of Companhia Ribeirao Grande, which until last week belonged to the Joao Santos group.
-- COTIA TRADING INAUGURATES ITS ARGENTINE PORT
The first Argentine port ever built buy private capital, Brazilian firm Cotia Trading's Terminal Zarate, was inaugurated yesterday. It will be used mainly to ship and unload automobiles.
O GLOBO
-- RIO IS LATIN AMERICA'S LARGEST BLACK-MARKET ARMS BUYER

Rio de Janeiro is Latin America's largest buyer of black-market arms, according to the U.S.'s Bureau of Alcohol, Tabacco and Firearms. A new U.S.-Brazil accord will allow U.S. agents to train Brazilians to combat illegal arms trafficking.
-- BRAZIL DEBT PAPER HAS RISEN 30 PCT IN DOLLARS
Those who bet on the Brazilian economy by buying the country's debt paper are seeing good profits. The value of the paper has risen 30 percent in dollar terms since the start of the year.
-- PRESIDENT CARDOSO PROMISES WATER FOR EVERYONE BY 1998
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso yesterday promised that all Brazilians who live in cities will have piped water by the end of his term in 1998. Today, just 76.2 percent have it.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- GOVERNMENT PLANS NEW REDUCTION IN INTEREST RATES
The Brazilian government is studying a new reduction in interest rates. In June, the monthly rate fell below 2 percent and may end this month at about 1.9 percent.
-- BUDGET CUT FOR JUDICIARY PROMPT CRISIS

A government proposal to cut the Brazilian judiciary's 1997 budget prompted a split between the courts and the government. Planning Minister Antonio Kandir and Supreme Federal Tribunal President Sepulveda Pertence began talks last night but failed to reach an accord.
-- MILITARY WILL APPEAL LAMARCA DECISION

Brazil's Military Club will appeal a government decision to compensate the families of leftist guerrillas Carlos Lamarca and Carlos Marighella, who were slain after being captured by the military in the early 1970s.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
